decision: tested the riskiest unknown first: can each model research a claim with only web tools and answer through in-process custom tools

decision: skipped the architect skill and wrote the design directly
why: the spike made the data shape concrete and storage is local and cheap to change; a design bakeoff would cost more than it saves

decision: the court record is an append-only event log, and the claim verdicts are a projection computed from it
why: one source of truth for both the replay page and the verdict badges; no second status field to keep in sync

decision: each turn exposes only the custom tools legal for that phase, through per-send customTools
why: the procedure state machine decides what an agent may do, so an illegal action cannot be called at all

decision: a worker crash mid-trial requeues the case and restarts the trial from an empty record
why: restarting from scratch converges to the same end state; resuming half-finished agent turns would be fragile

decision: tests for the 2-of-3 rule and the projection, then a full scripted session through the same validated tool path the real agents use
why: the judge path cannot be forced with real models, so the scripted court is what proves it

decision: broke the majority rule on purpose (2 to 3) to check the tests catch it

result: the 2 tests that depend on the rule failed; rule restored

decision: added a dismiss path so the judge can reject a submission with no verifiable claims
why: users will submit opinions; forcing claims out of them would produce fake verdicts

decision: ran a real session on the first case before building the site
